subject: Post-call: Veridian performance targets & acceptance plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Veridian performance targets & acceptance plan

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the p95/p99 targets and the test approach.

Recap (from our call)
- Veridian target: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 800ms end-to-end (inference + network) for production traffic profile.
- Current provider: you mentioned ~420ms p95 and ~920ms p99 during peak with ~600 RPS and ~12 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming behavior: many requests open as partial-chunk streaming (longer-lived connections), with spikes during batch jobs.

What Redwood needs from you to scope a hosted acceptance run:
1) A sample traffic profile (CSV) showing request size distribution, tokens per request, concurrency patterns.
2) A short list of representative streaming sessions (example payloads) so our SE can reproduce tail behavior.
3) A non-prod API key/access or allowlist IPs for a short side-by-side run.
4) Confirmation on data residency / egress constraints for logs during the test.

Proposed acceptance plan (high level)
- Side-by-side 72-hour run comparing Redwood hosted -> your production-shaped traffic.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 300ms AND p99 <= 800ms for steady-state traffic; no more than 5% request error budget over the window.
- Test matrices: throughput sweep (100 -> 600 RPS), streaming concurrency sweep (1 -> 20 concurrent streams), and spike test (10x burst for 60s).

Attachments: postcall-notes.pdf (short version of call notes and action items)

Can you confirm you can share the CSV + example payloads and whether next Wednesday (Jan 18) works to kick off the run? If you need an NDA/PO for a short evaluation talk to procurement, flag it and we’ll loop in Sales Ops.

Thanks — looping Marissa for the technical plan and Ben for commercial alignment.

—
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few data points and attaching our current metrics workbook.

Current metrics (prod, last 7d rolling)
- Peak throughput: ~600 RPS (sustained bursts to 800 RPS for short windows)
- p95 end-to-end: 420 ms
- p99 end-to-end: 920 ms
- Error rate: 0.7% (mostly timeouts during extreme spikes)
- Typical streaming concurrency: 8–12 active streams, occasional job windows with ~18.

Streaming specifics: our requests are chunked; each open connection keeps partial tokens flowing for up to ~12s while downstream enrichment returns. That pattern drives the long tail.

We can provide: veridian-current-metrics.xlsx (attached), and a sanitized sample_traffic_profile.csv.

As for schedule, Jan 18 is tight — we have a compliance audit that week. Would Jan 20–22 be possible? Also: we require logs that include anonymized request IDs and timestamps; we cannot allow external storage of raw customer payloads, but a hashed token/sample is fine. Please confirm Redwood’s ability to accept hashed payloads and keep logs in us-east region.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, Veridian Health
sara@veridian.ai

Sara — great context, thanks. I’m Marissa (Solutions Engineer) — I’ll own the test harness and run the side-by-side. A few clarifications and the procedural plan below.

Clarifications
- Hashed payloads are fine for the run; we only need token counts, prompt sizes, and streaming chunk behavior. Please provide the sample_traffic_profile.csv and 5 representative hashed streaming payloads.
- Logs: we will keep all logs scoped to us-east and redact payloads per your compliance notes. We will not persist raw customer content outside the test window.

Technical acceptance plan (detailed)
1) Prep (Day -3 to 0)
   - Exchange allowlist IPs and provide a short-lived test API key.
   - We sign a short PIA addendum (if you prefer) — Redwood legal can send a one-page doc.
   - Ingest sample_traffic_profile.csv and validate token distribution.
2) Run (72-hour window)
   - Baseline sweep: steady 100/250/400/600 RPS (4 x 6-hour blocks).
   - Streaming concurrency sweep: 1/5/10/15/20 concurrent simulated streams across baseline throughput.
   - Spike test: 10x burst for 60s at 24h mark to validate graceful degradation/fallbacks.
   - Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, connection open duration, per-token latency, error types.
3) Acceptance criteria
   - p95 <= 300ms AND p99 <= 800ms for steady-state buckets at target throughput; critical failures (5xx/timeouts) <= 0.5% during the run.
   - On regression flags, Redwood will provide packet traces and stack-level traces for triage; Veridian to provide sample request IDs for correlation.
4) Post-run
   - Deliver a report with time-series, tail-slice analysis, and recommended config (batching/quantization/profile).

Schedule
- Proposed kickoff: Mon Jan 22 09:00 PT (3-day prep starting Jan 19). If you can share the CSV and sample payloads by Jan 18 we can hit Jan 22.

Attachment: hosted-test-procedure.md (step-by-step test harness details).

If that looks reasonable I’ll provision the test pool and send the allowlist and key rotation plan. Ben — can you confirm if we need a commercial holdback / evaluation credit before running?

—
